entry.label: Boundary critique
entry.description: Ulrich's CSH examines motivation, power, knowledge, and legitimation. Comparing existing and proposed boundary judgements can expose whose version of improvement a claim serves; it does not compute the uniquely right boundary.
entry.canonical_definition: Critical examination of the judgements that make some facts, values, people, and consequences relevant to a claim while excluding or subordinating others.

profile.title: Boundary critique
profile.canonical_definition: Critical examination of the judgements that make some facts, values, people, and consequences relevant to a claim while excluding or subordinating others.
profile.summary: Ulrich's CSH examines motivation, power, knowledge, and legitimation. Comparing existing and proposed boundary judgements can expose whose version of improvement a claim serves; it does not compute the uniquely right boundary.
profile.why_it_matters: A technically defensible proposal may leave the people bearing its costs unable to question its purpose. Examining that exclusion changes what the proposal can legitimately claim.
key_distinctions: validity within an account versus legitimacy of its use for action
people involved in deciding versus people affected by the decision
asking what is the case versus asking what ought to be the case
surfacing a judgement versus settling it
historical_lineage: Ulrich's Critical Systems Heuristics; the normative focus is explicit in his author primer and 2022 account.
practice_connections: Take one claimed improvement. Name its beneficiary, measure of success, decision-maker, and person bearing a consequence outside that measure.
Change one of those judgements and identify which evidence or recommendation changes with it.
Record how those affected can challenge the premises, and who has authority to act on that challenge.
common_misreadings: Boundary critique is a stakeholder list or a wider diagram.
Completing twelve questions establishes the right boundary.
People attending an inquiry thereby authorise its conclusions.
One fixed ordering of is and ought questions is compulsory.
open_checks: The practice questions are editorial applications, not a replacement twelve-question framework.
A route for legitimate decision and contest remains necessary; the questions alone do not establish it.
profile.editorial_note: The previous profile was curator checked in August 2026. This proposed revision is a new research pass and carries no inherited human sign-off. Practical examples and the comparison with the observer are editorial applications.
